key_insight: LEADS uses an LLM agent to discover patient-specific hybrid cardiac electrophysiology models by searching over a structured set of physically grounded model-building actions, rather than relying on manually designed architectures.
engineering_relevance: This enables more transferable and interpretable digital twins for cardiac EP, with model structure adapted to each patient while preserving numerical stability for simulation.
method: Formulates cardiac EP domain knowledge as a structured action space for model discovery.
Runs an iterative reasoning-and-action loop to select, combine, and refine hybrid physics-neural structures.
Uses gradient descent only for parameter fitting after the architecture is chosen.
evidence_signal: The framework was validated on synthetic data with three ground-truth reaction models and on real cardiac EP data, where it outperformed human-designed hybrid models and other LLM-based methods.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the structured action space; if the search space is incomplete or biased, the agent may miss the best hybrid structure.
paper_title: Learning Cardiac Electrophysiology Digital Twins Through Agentic Discovery of Hybrid Structure
